title: Distractor Quality Score (DQS) Model v1.0
purpose: Standardized 0-100 score for distractor quality assessment. Implements CERTIFICATION_RUBRICS D4 (Distractor Quality) dimension with enhanced granularity.

rubric.30: Targets a specific, documented misconception. Requires genuine content knowledge to eliminate. Would fool a candidate holding that misconception.
rubric.22: Plausible but surface-level. Some test-taking strategies could help eliminate. Covers a real but shallow misconception.
rubric.15: Eliminable by test-taking tricks alone (length cueing, grammatical mismatch). Does not require content knowledge to dismiss.
rubric.5: Obviously wrong (absurd number, nonsensical concept, contradicts scenario facts). No candidate would genuinely select this.
rubric.0: 100% identical to another distractor or the correct answer. Non-functional.

rubric.20: Completely distinct from all other distractors and correct answer. Tests a unique misconception.
rubric.12: Mostly distinct. Minor overlap with another distractor but different misconception targeted.
rubric.5: Significant overlap (>70% Jaccard similarity) with another distractor. Tests nearly the same error.
rubric.0: 100% identical to another distractor or verbatim duplicate across items.

rubric.20: Maps to a documented CMA exam trap. Misconception is common among real candidates. EW text names and explains the error.
rubric.12: Maps to a plausible but less common error. EW text acknowledges a genuine misunderstanding.
rubric.5: Maps to a generic or vague error ('misapplied a concept'). EW text does not identify specific misconception.
rubric.0: No misconception targeted. Distractor is random, nonsensical, or impossible to reach by any error.

rubric.20: EW text teaches candidate why their choice was wrong, names the governing standard, shows correct reasoning, and provides a memory anchor.
rubric.12: EW text explains why the choice was wrong but lacks standard reference or contrast with correct approach.
rubric.5: EW text is present but generic ('Option X is incorrect'). No teaching content.
rubric.0: EW text is empty, boilerplate template, or factually wrong.

rubric.10: Would discriminate between candidates at different proficiency levels. Advanced candidates recognize the trap; weaker candidates fall for it.
rubric.6: Moderate discrimination. Separates strong from weak candidates but doesn't distinguish mid-level.
rubric.3: Low discrimination. Both strong and weak candidates either both get it right or both get it wrong.
rubric.0: No discrimination — everyone gets it right (obviously wrong) or everyone gets it wrong (unfairly tricky).

aggregation.item_dqs: Average DQS of all distractors in the item
aggregation.section_dqs: Average of item DQS in the section
aggregation.pack_dqs: Average of section DQS weighted by item count
aggregation.portfolio_dqs: Average of pack DQS weighted by item count

certification_threshold: Item DQS >= 60 required (maps to CERTIFICATION_RUBRICS D4 >= 4). Pack-level DQS < 60 indicates sections needing targeted distractor remediation before certification.
